newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Eurostocks mixed, dlr up on US rate prospects.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Eurostocks mixed, dlr up on US rate prospects.

text.p: European bourses were mixed on Monday as investors became increasingly alarmed that the United States might increase interest rates for the first time in two years.
But on currency markets the the prospect of higher rates boosted the dollar against the mark and yen as traders anticipated a more attractive return on dollar-denominated assets.

Frankfurt stocks closed with healthy gains but London fell sharply in nervous trading ahead of Tuesday's meeting of the U.S. central bank's policy-making Federal Open Market Committee, which is widely expected to raise rates.
The uncertain mood on European markets followed volatile trading last week after hints by U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan about an impending rise in U.S. interest rates.

London's FTSE index of leading shares fell 0.75 percent, its lowest level for two months and the sixth consecutive trading session to register losses. By midafternoon, the FTSE was down 32.3 points at 4222.5, drawing no comfort from a strong start in New York.
"Well, we needed some sort of correction and we are certainly getting it," said one dealer. "The market has become very nervous, we may come back to 4,150 as part of this correction."
The index tumbled 3.8 percent last week as investors braced themselves for the upcoming British general election and the possibility of near-term interest rate rises at home and in the United States.
Traders do not expect to see a British rate rise until after the election in May but investors are increasingly worried that the FOMC will be tempted to increase interest rates on Tuesday.

"If there is going to be a change, it should be no more than a quarter point," said one dealer. "If it's higher the market will be disappointed and if there is no change at all we will continue in this period of uncertainty."
In contrast, Frankfurt closed up 0.72 percent, shrugging aside the rates worries and taking encouragement from the stronger dollar, seen as good news for the exporting sector.
"The market is surprisingly strong... the main factor is that the market has factored in a 25-basis point hike in U.S. interest rates," one trader said.
In Paris, shares climbed at the opening but later slipped in and out of profit as investors focused attention on the FOMC meeting and optimism ebbed away.
Among individual stocks, Lyonnaise des Eaux rose 2.67 percent to 576 francs and Suez was up 2.4 percent at 287.10 following newspaper reports the two were preparing a merger.
On the currency front, the dollar was trading more strongly with analysts also predicting a 25 basis point hike in the key Fed funds rate at Tuesday's FOMC meeting.

"A 25 basis point hike has already been priced in... The increase we're looking for tomorrow would be seen as the first of a number of increases," said Julian Fisher, international economist at Daiwa Europe in London.
But a discordant note for the dollar was struck by a senior Bundesbank official who expressed concern about the effect a U.S. rate hike would have on German rates.

Bundesbank council member Ernst Welteke said an increase in U.S. rates could push German rates higher, adding that this "cannot be desirable". He said the central bank considered the level of German rates appropriate now in view of current inflation, the economic situation, and money supply.

"The (Welteke) comments... were slightly deutschemark-supportive, but the main backdrop is dollar-supportive based on the expectations of higher interest rates tomorrow," said Tim Fox, treasury economist at Standard Chartered.
CURRENCIES AT 1530 GMT
The dollar was trading at 1.6897 marks and 122.90 yen compared with 1.6835 marks and 122.55 yen in late European trade on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1530 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 36.4 points at 4,218.4.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was down 7.14 points at 2,579.99.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index ended up 23.60 points at 3,321.84.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed in the afternoon at $350.20 an ounce, against London's close of $352.65 on Friday. Silver was at $5.14, down four cents.
